newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli soldier wounded in south Lebanon fighting.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier wounded in south Lebanon fighting.

text.p: An Israeli soldier and two Lebanese civilians were wounded on Sunday when Israeli forces and Moslem guerrillas exchanged fire in south Lebanon, witnesses and pro-Israeli sources said.
Pro-Israeli militia sources said the soldier was wounded in Sojoud area on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
In Beirut, a spokesman for the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God), said the group's guerrillas had killed several Israeli soldiers in the Sojoud fighting.
"The Islamic resistance attacked an Israeli unit in Sojoud and several Zionist soldiers were killed and several were wounded," he said.
"Israeli helicopters tried to rescue the injured but they failed. There is heavy fighting and the Israeli helicopters have carried out many raids on Sojoud," the spokesman added.
There was no immediate confirmation of any Israeli deaths from the pro-Israeli militia sources.
The sources reported heavy clashes and said Hizbollah fighters were coming under machinegun fire from Israeli helicopters.
Witnesses said two villagers were wounded when Israeli artillery pounded Iqlim al-Toufah -- rugged mountainland north of Sojoud used by Hizbollah guerrillas to attack the Israeli zone.
They said a seven-year-old boy sustained an eye injury in the shelling and a 24-year-old man was slightly wounded in the arm.
Hizbollah guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide border zone they hold in south Lebanon.

Israel has held the border strip uninterruptedly since its first invasion of Lebanon in 1978. It set the current boundaries of the zone in 1985 after withdrawing the bulk of its forces following a second invasion in 1982.
